goal: Ratify the exact all-adapter local runtime, continuation, orchestration, context, configuration, and delivery contract.
description: Scope: Requirements.md and the existing client-release agent/routing requirements. Context: the current release-owned contract permits an empty supported subset and omits path-based context, target budgets, framework compression, and adapter hot reload. Target: establish REQ-001 through REQ-016 as the single final product state and define all agents as the exact canonical manifest set. Design Considerations: separate product capability from release publication, keep framework capability gaps fail-closed, and preserve server authority outside the client. Design Value: prevents implementation from redefining all-adapter completion or treating honest exclusion as delivery. Constraints & Risks: no fixture-only readiness, no layout redesign, no store/publication claim, and no sensitive runtime evidence.

acceptance_criteria.text: Requirements.md defines users, workflows, exact all-adapter scope, functional and non-functional constraints, non-goals, and final acceptance for REQ-001 through REQ-016.
The contract states that no blocked, unverified, excluded, or send-disabled canonical adapter can satisfy final all-adapter acceptance.

goal: Implement one bounded session supervisor and ordered event authority for all official transport drivers.
description: Scope: native agent_runtime session supervisor, conversation lane/runtime adapters, turn event emission, Dart AgentDispatchLane/AgentConversationService contracts, and lifecycle tests. Context: exact-ID and streaming checks exist but process maps, active handles, readiness, and driver lifecycle are not one bounded authority. Target: supervise open/resume/send/stream/cancel/timeout/cleanup with revision pinning, monotonic sequence ownership, exact native identity, global and per-adapter limits, drain, and unknown-outcome semantics. goal: Implement schema-validated atomic adapter and routing configuration reload with last-good and drain semantics.
description: Scope: native adapter configuration store/watcher, routing policy store integration, portable-data resolution, immutable registry revisions, generated config documentation, and reload tests. Context: routing policy hot reload exists, but transport/readiness configuration is compiled or scattered. Target: use one product-relative configuration tree, parse off-path, exact-set validate, atomically queue a revision, apply it at a message boundary, retain last-good on failure, and drain removed adapters. Design Considerations: Repository plus immutable snapshot, debounce, revision digest, O(1) lookup, and bounded watcher/cache lifecycle. Design Value: adapters can be configured and refreshed without rebuild while active conversations remain stable. Constraints & Risks: no secrets or raw runtime data in portable files; invalid input and symlink/path escape fail closed; retired config locations are removed.

acceptance_criteria.text: Valid adapter/routing edits activate once at a message boundary; invalid, partial, duplicate, secret-bearing, or path-escaping edits preserve the last-good snapshot.

goal: Implement target-aware context budgeting and private digest-bound local context artifacts.
description: Scope: context budget/artifact domain modules, private filesystem adapter, dispatch context reference contract, route history projection, cleanup, and tests. Context: routed context is currently inline JSON and bounded by global approximations rather than the target model. Target: resolve target/model limits and reserves, select required source sections in O(n), decide fit/overflow deterministically, atomically write a private immutable package, pass a typed path/digest reference through stdin/protocol, require acknowledgement, and clean it within bounded lifetime. Design Considerations: content digest, opaque handles, no-follow private files, exact byte/token accounting where available, conservative manifest bounds otherwise, and O(1) artifact lookup. Design Value: makes handoff explicit and scalable while preventing unbounded prompt copies and path disclosure. Constraints & Risks: path never enters argv/UI/log/evidence; unknown budget, digest mismatch, unacknowledged artifact, symlink escape, or cleanup escape fails closed.

acceptance_criteria.text: Boundary tests prove exact fit/overflow decisions for target limits/reserves and reject unknown, underestimated, oversized, or required-section-losing packages.
Private path creation, typed stdin/protocol reference, digest acknowledgement, redaction, TTL/terminal cleanup, no-follow behavior, and bounded artifact state pass positive and adversarial tests.

goal: Implement framework-executed bounded hierarchical compression with fidelity and content-addressed caching.
description: Scope: compression broker/domain, manifest compression capabilities, policy selection, existing distillation broker integration, bounded cache, audit projection, and tests. Context: current distillation calls an agent but uses one fixed input window and does not bind a destination budget or context path. Target: select a ready compression-capable framework, dispatch compression through the supervised lane, preserve required sections, hierarchically compress oversized sources with fixed fan-out/retry limits, validate fidelity, and cache passing output by complete semantic revision key. Design Considerations: chronological chunk plan, content-addressed O(1) cache, byte/count LRU bounds, alternate compressor only after known failure, and immutable artifacts. Design Value: avoids repeated computation and enables large-context handoff without silent truncation. Constraints & Risks: no local heuristic summary may impersonate framework compression; failure, missing capability, insufficient reduction, or fidelity loss prevents destination dispatch.

acceptance_criteria.text: Tests prove target overflow selects the declared ready framework, bounded hierarchical compression preserves required sections, and fidelity or reduction failure blocks dispatch.
Cache hit, eviction, revision/model/budget invalidation, bounded memory/disk use, cancellation, and minimum redacted audit evidence are verified.

goal: Complete deterministic strategy planning and bounded DAG scheduling over the supervised runtime and context pipeline.
description: Scope: routing policy schema/planner/evaluator, new scheduler module, route coordinator/bindings/history, failure and result contracts, and tests. Context: strategy execution exists in controller actions with a fixed parallel cap, while context preparation, semaphores, cancellation, and failure aggregation are not one scheduler. Target: compile policy into an immutable DAG, use indegree plus stable ready ordering, enforce global/per-adapter concurrency, prepare one budgeted artifact per target, preserve exact branch sessions, and aggregate real results with explicit known/unknown outcomes. Design Considerations: O(V+E) topology, priority queue ordered by policy index, semaphores, cancellation tree, circuit/allowance snapshots, and message-boundary policy revision. Design Value: separates pure selection from lifecycle execution and makes all strategies predictable and testable. Constraints & Risks: no unsafe fallback after unknown outcome, no unbounded worker history, and no controller-owned process or session path.

acceptance_criteria.text: Deterministic tests cover every strategy, topology, stable tie-break, role/capability/readiness/allowance/circuit changes, message-boundary reload, and exact branch session reuse.
Stress and fake-lane tests prove bounded global/per-adapter concurrency, backpressure, cancellation, cleanup, real result aggregation, and no retry/fallback after unknown outcome.
